chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him saying: The opinion and the dream of a believer in the latter part of the time are a seventieth part of the parts of the Prophethood.

key_terms.آخِرِ الزَّمَانِ: The latter part of time / later era

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a believer's opinion and dreams in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) states that the opinion (رأي) and dreams (رؤيا) of a believer in the later era constitute one-seventieth of the total parts of Prophethood, indicating a high degree of spiritual insight and authority. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, highlights the concept of 'minor prophethood' (نبوة صغرى) or continuation of revelation (وحي) to the pious in the absence of the Prophet, a key theme in Shia eschatology regarding the heightened spiritual status of the faithful during the Great Occultation.

en.hubeali: H 14506 – Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hashaam Bin Saalim, who has narrated:
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The opinion and the dream of a ‘Momin’ (Believer), and what he sees in the later portion of the time is a seventieth part of the parts of the Prophet-hood’.
en.sarwar: 58. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hashaam Bin Saalim, who has narrated: ‘I heard Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying: ‘
The opinion and the dream of a ‘Momin’ (Believer), and what he sees in the later portion of the time is a seventieth part of the parts of the Prophet-hood’.
